baseline_prompt_en: A documentary photograph from a fictional military story, showing a woman military service member preparing a portable field radio for departure at a rough workshop bench inside a canvas equipment shelter just before dawn. Her facial appearance follows the supplied portrait: a softly rounded face, dark brown eyes, fine dark eyebrows, a small rounded nose, gently full pink lips, and a smooth short dark bob with separated wispy bangs. The portrait guides face and hair appearance only. She stands squarely behind the waist-high bench in olive field fatigues with the collar loosened by ordinary work, her quietly absorbing concentration lending the scene a subtle personal warmth. Her left hand holds the rugged olive radio upright at lower chest height, with her thumb bracing its side and the palm supporting its base. Her right hand grips a rectangular replacement battery and slides it down the exposed guide rails on the radio's rear; the battery is halfway seated, its lower edge visibly engaged with the rails and its upper edge still projecting above the radio body. The two wrists and both forearms remain visible and connect naturally to her shoulders. A second, removed battery rests flat on the bench beside the open padded equipment case, making the maintenance state readable. She watches the battery meet its rail with lowered eyes and slightly parted lips. A packed rucksack and a folded route map occupy the far end of the bench, while the open shelter flap reveals cool first light and the blurred shape of a waiting utility vehicle. Compose a vertical medium photograph from just above the bench to above her head, from her right front quarter so her face and the radio's rear rail connection share a readable view. The hands, battery and radio are together in the foreground focal plane, with the face close behind them and sharp enough for facial comparison. Soft blue dawn entering the flap meets a warm task lamp across the radio housing and her cheek; restrained grain, realistic skin and scuffed equipment surfaces preserve the unglamorous material effort of getting ready. The frame's visual order is the connected hands and half-seated battery, her attentive face, then the ready gear and opening toward departure.
